In a landmark decision, the NTCA declared Gujarat as a "Tiger Presence State" for the All India Tiger Estimation (AITE) 2026. This return to the tiger map follows the stable, permanent presence of a four-year-old tiger in the Ratanmahal Wildlife Sanctuary (Dahod district), marking the first time the state has been officially included since its removal in 1992.

Further Insights:

The last time a tiger census was conducted in Gujarat was in 1989, where only pugmarks (footprints) were found.

Because no tigers were sighted for several years, Gujarat was removed from the official tiger map in 1992.

This sanctuary, primarily known for Sloth Bears, is where the current tiger has established its territory.

The Dholki is the primary rhythmic instrument that provides the powerful and fast-paced beats essential for a Lavani dance performance.

• Lavani originated as a folk performance for entertainment and social messaging.

• It is traditionally performed to Marathi songs with strong rhythmic patterns.

• Lavani dancers synchronize footwork and expressions closely with drum beats.

• The Dholki is commonly used in Tamasha theatre traditions as well.

The Beveridge Curve shows an inverse relationship between the unemployment rate and the job vacancy rate.

When unemployment is high, vacancies are usually low.

When vacancies are high, unemployment tends to be low.

This curve is used to study labour market efficiency and matching between workers and jobs.

Phillips Curve

Shows the relationship between inflation and unemployment, not vacancies.

Laffer Curve

Shows the relationship between tax rates and tax revenue.

Lorenz Curve

Shows income or wealth inequality in an economy.

Further Insights

• An outward shift of the Beveridge Curve indicates worsening labour market efficiency.

• It is widely used in labour economics and macroeconomic analysis.

• High unemployment with high vacancies suggests skill mismatch.

• The curve is especially studied after economic shocks or recessions.

• It complements the Phillips Curve in analysing employment dynamics.

questions.question: In the following question, one of the parts of the sentence may have error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If the sentence is free from error, select answer option accordingly. The organizer and event manager have (1)/ stated that it is compulsory for all the staff members (2)/ to be present on the fifth of next week. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.questionHtml:
In the following question, one of the parts of the sentence may have error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If the sentence is free from error, select answer option accordingly.

The organizer and event manager have (1)/ stated that it is compulsory for all the staff members (2)/ to be present on the fifth of next week. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution:
The error lies in option (b).

When only the first subject is preceded by an article, the verb agreeing with it will be singular as we are talking about the same person.

For example: The Collector and Magistrate is expected to come soon. (Here, the Collector and Magistrate is the same person.)

Similarly, in this question, the use of a single article (The) implies that the 'organizer and event manager' is a single person. So, the verb that must agree with it must also be singular. Thus, 'have' in part (1) of the sentence must be replaced by 'has'.

Thus, the error is in option (b) 1.

Therefore, the corrected form of the sentence is: The organizer and event manager has stated that it is compulsory for all the staff members to be present on the fifth of next week.

Additional Information:

When each of the two subjects is preceded by an article, the verb agreeing with it will be plural as we are talking about two different individuals or things.

For example: The Prime minister and the President have arrived. (Here, the Prime Minister and the President are two different persons.)

questions.solution:
When we use 'if conditional' to talk about permanent truths, such as scientific facts, and general habits. The structure is if + present simple, present simple.

Therefore, the conditional tense 'would get' is grammatically incorrect. Option (b) is eliminated as it is not in the present simple tense [it is also in the conditional tense]. Note: Subject-Verb Agreement: Matching up singular or plural subjects with singular or plural forms of a verb is part of the process called agreement. questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. Had you studied English well for the exam?
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

Had you studied English well for the exam?

options.text: Had English studied well for the exam by you?
options.html: Had English studied well for the exam by you?

options.text: Had been studied English well for the exam by you?
options.html: Had been studied English well for the exam by you?

options.html: Has English studied well for the exam by you?

options.text: Had English been studied well for the exam by you?
options.html: Had English been studied well for the exam by you?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option (d).

The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a 'to be' form of the verb ['been' here] is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

The preposition "by" is used before the object made in Passive Voice. However, it is optional in some cases.

The question in Active voice is an interrogative sentence. The answer to this question will be either "yes" or "no".

These types of sentences usually begin with a helping verb like:
Have
Has
Had

The format of the sentence which begins with "Have", "Has" or "Had" in Active voice is: Have/Has/Had + Subject + V3 + Object?

Therefore, in Passive voice, the format will be: Have/Has/Had + Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + been + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).

For example:

Has Rohit written the letter? (Active)

Has the letter been written by Rohit? (Passive)

The options except (d) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Thus, the correct answer is: Had English been studied well for the exam by you?

questions.solution:
The tense of the sentence is never changed while converting the sentence from passive to active voice, and vice versa.

The sentence is in passive voice and in the past perfect tense (had been + V3).

Option a) is incorrect as it turns the sentence into the present perfect tense (has + V3).

Option b) is incorrect as it changes the tense into simple past tense (S + V2 + O).

Option c) is incorrect as it changes the tense into past continuous tense (Was + V1 + ing).

Only option d) contains the sentence with the structure for the sentence in past perfect tense, and in active voice, i.e., (had + V3).

Hence, option d) is correct.

questions.solution:
The sentence in the Indirect Speech is in Past Perfect Continuous Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Direct Speech will be in Present Perfect Continuous Tense.

Past Perfect Continuous (Subject + had been + V1 + ing + Object) will be converted into Present Perfect Continuous (Subject + has/have been + V1 + ing + Object).

For example:

Leela said that the kids had been quarrelling for hours. (Indirect Speech)

Leela said, "The kids have been quarrelling for hours" (Direct Speech)

The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech:

Indirect SpeechDirect Speech
told... thatsaid to
theyYou
had been usinghave been using

Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

Note: There is a second case as well where the past perfect continuous tense (indirect speech) changes to Past continuous (direct speech).

In such questions involving more than one case, we go with the options. Since options do not include the sentence in past continuous tense, option (d) is the right answer.

questions.solution:
In the case of Interrogative sentences like this, "said" in Direct Speech is changed into "enquired (of)", "wanted to know", "asked", etc.

In Indirect speech, the verb is always placed after the subject, unlike in Direct Speech.

For example:

The teacher said to him, "What is your name?" (Direct Speech)

The teacher asked him what his name was. (Indirect Speech)

Also, the sentence in the Direct Speech is in the Present Simple tense. So, the tense in the Indirect Speech should be in the Past Simple tense.

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

· The reporting verb 'said to' is changed into 'asked'.

· The verb 'don't' (present simple) is changed into 'did not' (past simple).

· The pronoun 'you' is changed into 'I'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Carol asked me why I did not have any qualifications.

questions.question: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. This reduces the effort of farmers as well as the cost of farming. B. So, the Centre feels that considering the cost-effectiveness, its cultivation can be expanded in India. C. The Centre has decided to promote the cultivation of dragon fruit for its health benefits. D. According to the Indian Council of Agriculture Research, the fruit plant doesn't need much water and can be cultivated on dry land, too.
questions.questionHtml:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. This reduces the effort of farmers as well as the cost of farming.

B. So, the Centre feels that considering the cost-effectiveness, its cultivation can be expanded in India.

C. The Centre has decided to promote the cultivation of dragon fruit for its health benefits.

D. According to the Indian Council of Agriculture Research, the fruit plant doesn't need much water and can be cultivated on dry land, too.
questions.solution:
Sentence A does not come first, as a prior context is required to understand what 'this' refers to.

Sentence C comes first as it introduces us to the main subject 'the cultivation of dragon fruit' and also provides a platform to carry forward the discussion. Sentence D states that the fruit plant doesn't need much water and can be cultivated on dry land. Because of these reasons, the effort and cost of farming are very low (sentence A). Sentence B starts with 'so', which can be used to introduce clauses of result or decision (that's why it does not come first in the sequence, implying it follows some prior discussion). A mentions the benefit, and B mentions the decision the Centre has taken because of such benefits. So, B follows A. Therefore, CDAB becomes the correct order among the given options. Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.
